stops.before: Alexander has conquered the world and Greek is its language. Jews in Jerusalem and Alexandria write wisdom for a people who now argue with philosophers.
stops.watch: Sirach's grandson translated his grandfather's book: practical wisdom on friends, money, daughters and doctors, and chapter 24, Wisdom speaking of herself as the Law. The Book of Wisdom, in Greek from Alexandria: the souls of the just 'are in the hand of God', and the righteous man whom the wicked plot to kill — a page the Passion narrative echoes.
stops.after: A Greek king decides the Jews will be Greeks too.

stops.before: Antiochus IV Epiphanes forbids circumcision and Sabbath, and sacrifices a pig on the altar of the Temple — 'the abomination of desolation'.
stops.watch: An old priest in Modein kills the king's officer and the collaborator at the altar, and his five sons take to the hills; Judas 'the Hammer' wins battle after battle; the Temple cleansed and rededicated — Hanukkah. 2 Maccabees 7: the mother and her seven sons, the first clear statement of the resurrection of the body. Daniel 7–12, the visions, belong to these years.
stops.after: The Maccabees' heirs quarrel, Rome is invited in, and Pompey walks into the Holy of Holies. Sixty years later, in a client king's reign, Gabriel is sent to a village in Galilee.
